title: Peritia method contract
description: A method definition states what one executable method computes and when its result holds. tools/method_contract.py adds the checks a schema cannot express.

name.description: An input name: lower case, digits and underscores.

id.description: A method or skill identifier: lower case, digits and hyphens.

unit.description: Lexical filter for a case-sensitive UCUM symbol (1 to 32 printable ASCII characters, excluding spaces). The loader does not parse UCUM.

evidence_path.description: The path of one entry of the slot result's evidence list.

quantity.description: The physical quantity, for example electric current.

required.description: Whether a run may start without this value.

bound.description: Where the method's result holds for one input, in that input's unit. Both ends are inclusive. Comparisons use IEEE 754 binary64 for decimal and exponent JSON tokens (RFC 8259, section 6) and integers for integer tokens. For example, 0.80000000000000001 reads as 0.8 and meets a 0.8 point bound.

skill.description: The skill directory under skills/ that teaches this method.

task.description: The one concrete task the method supports.

conventions.description: Sign, coordinate and time conventions the inputs and outputs follow.

implementation.description: The tool that runs the method, at one exact version.

version.description: A normalized PEP 440 public version or a full 40-digit lowercase hexadecimal revision hash.

verifier.description: The executable check of a result and the condition it accepts.

command.description: The argument list, first item the program.

result_class.description: What kind of claim a result of this method is.
